Jersey Mike’s $JMKE reported second-quarter revenue of $208 million, up 10%, in its first quarterly results since its Blackstone-backed initial public offering.

The Details:

•	Profit decline: Net income fell to $37 million for the quarter ended June 28 from $59 million a year earlier. 

•	Comparable sales: Same-store sales grew 2.3%, driven primarily by higher transactions. 

•	Store expansion: The chain opened 83 stores, grew net units 8.1% year over year, and ended the quarter with 3,378 locations. 

•	Sales outlook: Jersey Mike’s projects full-year same-store-sales growth of 2.5% to 3% and current-quarter growth of 3% to 4%.

Google $GOOGL will invest at least €13 billion, or $15.11 billion, in Finnish AI infrastructure, data centers, and clean-energy projects during 2027 and 2028.

The Details:

•	European investment: Google called the commitment its largest single investment in Europe.

•	Site expansion: Funding will support the existing Hamina data center and projects across four Finnish locations for Gemini, Search, Maps, and YouTube.

•	Economic impact: Google expects initial construction to support more than 37,000 jobs, with operational facilities projected to support 7,000 jobs.

•	Power agreement: Fortum $FORTUM signed a 22-year agreement for Google to buy 50% of Loviisa nuclear capacity from 2030 through 2049.

Xanadu $XNDU and ASML $ASML launched a collaboration to develop advanced lithography processes for Xanadu’s photonic quantum hardware and reduce optical losses in quantum chips.

The Details:

•	Technical focus: The companies will explore process approaches intended to improve patterning control and create lower-loss photonic structures. 

•	Loss challenge: Optical loss is a key technical obstacle to fault-tolerant, error-corrected photonic quantum hardware. 

•	Process factor: The collaboration will examine line-edge roughness, which lithography and related process conditions can influence.

Amazon $AMZN began selling sterling bonds Wednesday in its first British-pound offering as hyperscalers diversify funding for AI infrastructure investment.

The Details:

•	Bond tranches: The four-part offering includes three-, six-, 12-, and 19-year maturities and was scheduled to price later Wednesday. 

•	Initial pricing: Guidance ranged from about 70 basis points over U.K. government bonds for three-year debt to 110 basis points for 19-year debt.

•	Funding markets: Sterling follows Amazon’s prior euro and Swiss-franc bond issuance.

•	Sector borrowing: Hyperscalers have issued more than $200 billion of debt this year, exceeding twice their full-year 2025 issuance, according to LSEG data.

Unusual Machines $UMAC announced an additional $20 million strategic investment in Xtend AI Robotics $XTND, raising its total investment to $27.5 million.

The Details:

•	Financing structure: The $20 million investment is part of Xtend’s $110 million financing, which closed with its business combination and NYSE listing.

•	Existing relationship: Xtend is an existing Unusual Machines customer, and the companies describe their relationship as both supplier and strategic partner.

•	Investment focus: Unusual Machines said the investment supports its strategy of deploying capital across the drone ecosystem and complementary technologies.

•	Defense market: Xtend said it is focused on NDAA-compliant, American-made Physical AI systems for U.S. and allied defense customers.

HP $HPQ, NVIDIA $NVDA, and Red Hat launched an enterprise platform for local AI inference built around HP’s orderable ZGX Fury workstation.

The Details:

•	Compute system: HP ZGX Fury uses NVIDIA’s GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip and targets up to 20 FP4 petaFLOPS of AI performance.

•	Software stack: The workstation is certified for Red Hat Enterprise Linux and supports OpenShift, NVIDIA AI Enterprise, and CUDA.

•	Local inference: HP positions the system to address latency, privacy, sovereignty, and connectivity requirements for enterprise AI workloads.

•	Target sectors: The companies target manufacturing, healthcare, government, retail, and development environments.

Firefly $FLY signed a multi-launch agreement with SSC Space for two Alpha rocket missions from Sweden’s Esrange Space Center, targeted no earlier than 2028.

The Details:

•	Customer missions: The launches will serve Swedish national-security customers and additional commercial rideshare customers.

•	Payload capacity: SSC Space secured the full payload capacity for both missions and can allocate space among government and commercial customers.

•	Launch infrastructure: The partners completed a launch control center, payload-processing facility, integration building, tracking systems, and security facilities at Esrange.
